content.content:
Never-Sold: "The Chainbreakers buy out Owings, debts paid in work, at what they were first set. There is a woman north of Blackrose called Rows-For-Another. Eleven years ago she damaged one of an estate's boats. The estate's steward assessed her an Owing of four months' work. She works it still. I have put by what that Owing was at first: one hundred gold. By custom an Owing paid at its first price is closed. It is never mentioned again. Take the coin. If you can talk the steward round without it, keep it. From here take the swamp road north out of Blackrose. The channel bank is a short walk on. The steward Hulm-Tei stands there with his book. Hear what Rows-For-Another wants before you do anything."
Quest started: Four Months for a Boat
Journal entry (Four Months for a Boat): Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, told me of Rows-For-Another. Never-Sold gave me the Owing's first price, 100 gold, to pay if I must; it is mine to keep if words do the work instead. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank, a short walk north of Blackrose along the swamp road, where Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, stands with his book.

content.content:
Rows-For-Another: "Never-Sold would do that for me? Then I will take it. Look at my skin. Eleven years away from my tree has turned it grey. I want to go home before it greys further. It is slow, and I will not pretend otherwise. Hulm-Tei keeps the book with my page in it. He must be paid the first price or talked round before he will strike it. I will say no more of him, because he is standing there and he can hear us. When the page is struck, the old custom closes the Owing for good. It is never spoken of again. It frees me. It does not change how the estate treats the next one held. Hulm-Tei will give you the page. Take it down the swamp road to Never-Sold in Blackrose."
